details: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East, particularly military exchanges between Saudi Arabia and Houthi forces in Yemen, has heightened tensions along crucial transportation routes, threatening global energy resource flow. In response, China has reportedly intervened, urging Iran to pressure the rebels to curb attacks on oil infrastructure. Despite diplomatic efforts, tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz remains significantly reduced, impacting crude oil prices.
title: Middle East Tensions Escalate, China Engages on Oil Route Security

details: The U.S. Federal Reserve has raised its policy interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to a target range of 3.75% to 4%, marking the first rate hike in over three years. This decision, aimed at curbing inflation fueled in part by rising crude oil prices due to the Middle East crisis, was made despite political pressure. The Fed indicated the possibility of further rate hikes this year, reinforcing market beliefs of a continued restrictive monetary policy.
sourceName: XTB.com / (Also reported by various financial news outlets, citing the Fed)
title: Fed Hikes Rates Amid Inflation Concerns, Signals Further Tightening

details: Despite renewed concerns about inflation, rising borrowing costs, and hawkish shifts from global central banks (including the Fed and Bank of Japan), Bitcoin's price has surpassed the $80,000 mark. The digital asset market is showing widespread optimism, with investors seemingly viewing the tightening monetary policies as already "fully priced in."
title: Bitcoin Breaks $80,000 Despite Hawkish Central Banks

details: News that a U.S. regulator is facilitating the trading of tokenized shares of traditional companies has significantly boosted sentiment in the digital asset market. Following this development, Ethereum (ETH) notably jumped by 6%, as the SEC's approval directly impacts the utility and integration of public blockchains for traditional financial assets.
sourceName: Pluang / (Also reported by various crypto news outlets)
title: US Regulator Greenlights Tokenized Stock Trading on Blockchains

details: The U.S. Senate voted to block the CLARITY Act from advancing, falling short of the required 60 votes. This legislative effort aimed to provide clearer regulatory guidelines for the cryptocurrency industry. Despite being considered "objectively bad news" for regulatory clarity, Bitcoin's price remained relatively resilient, suggesting the market had either priced in the outcome or displayed strong underlying support.
title: Senate Fails to Pass CLARITY Act, Regulatory Uncertainty Persists
